data.name: Aqra
data.gender_notes: Aqra is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic root ‘aqr’ meaning ‘to read’ or ‘to recite’. This name is given to a child who is expected to become a scholar, a reader of the Quran or a wise and knowledgeable person. The name Aqra carries the meaning “Reader or Scholar” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Aqra usually hope their child will grow to embody reader or scholar and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name of wisdom and knowledge.
data.etymology: Aqra belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Reader or Scholar.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aqra total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_arabic.name: أقرا
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و معناه: الأكثر قراءة، الأكثر تعلماً، والأقرأ هو الشخص الذي يقرأ كثيرًا ويتعلم الكثير، وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في سورة العلق: «أَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي يَأْمُرُ بِالْعَدْلِ وَهُوَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ كَفِيلٌ» كلمة أقرأ تعني أن يقرأ الإنسان القرآن ويتعلمه ويحفظه.

in_urdu.name: اقرا
in_urdu.meaning: بیشتر پڑھنے والا، زیادہ علم رکھنے والا
in_urdu.long_meaning: اقرا ایک مذکر اسم ہے جس کا مطلب ہے زیادہ پڑھنے والا، زیادہ علم رکھنے والا، اور یہ نام عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے۔اس کا مطلب ہے کہ جو شخص زیادہ قرآن پڑھتا ہے اور زیادہ علم رکھتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: अقرा
in_hindi.meaning: ज्यादा पढ़ने वाला, अधिक जानने वाला
in_hindi.long_meaning: अقرा एक पुल्लिंग नाम है जिसका अर्थ है ज्यादा पढ़ने वाला, अधिक जानने वाला। यह नाम अरबी भाषा से लिया गया है और इसका अर्थ है वह व्यक्ति जो अधिक कुरआन पढ़ता है और अधिक ज्ञान रखता है।

in_pashto.name: اقرا
in_pashto.long_meaning: اقرا د یو مذکر نوم دی چې معنی یې ډیر لوستونکی، ډیر پوهیږی، او دا نوم د عربي ژبې څخه اخیستل شوی دی. دا نوم د هغه چا لپاره کارول کیږي چې ډیر قرآن لوستي او ډیر علم ولري.

in_english.name: Aqra
in_english.long_meaning: Aqra is a masculine given name of Arabic origin, meaning 'most reader' or 'most knowledgeable'. It is derived from the Arabic root 'q-r-ʾ' which means 'to read' or 'to recite'. In Islamic tradition, the name Aqra signifies a person who is well-versed in the Quran and Islamic studies. Historically, the name has been used to describe individuals who are renowned for their knowledge and piety.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Aqra' holds a significant cultural importance as it is often given to children in Islamic communities who are held in high regard for their intellectual abilities, academic achievements and dedication to learning. Those named 'Aqra' have a responsibility to acquire knowledge, especially in the Quran and Hadith, and contribute to the development and preservation of their culture.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name 'Aqra' is bestowed upon a child as a reminder of the importance of knowledge and understanding in Islam. It is believed that Allah rewards those who seek knowledge and wisdom, and the name 'Aqra' serves as a constant inspiration and motivation for the bearer to strive for knowledge and dignity in all aspects of their life. Furthermore, the name symbolizes the continuation of theological and intellectual knowledge passed down through generations, emphasizing the role of education and scholarship in promoting the teachings and values of Islam.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Aqra ibn Hisham was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad. The name Aqra carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Aqra ibn Hisham was a prominent companion of the Prophet Muhammad during his lifetime. He was known for his generosity and was one of the first converts to Islam in the city of Mecca. He also participated in several major battles, including the Battle of Badr and the Battle of Uhud.
